positive: Cited repeatedly as a counter-example in the refund-complaint thread — commenters describe their own Capitol Residences cancellations being refunded without issue — and separately credited with a better lift-to-flat ratio than Edition and other nearby projects.
Capitol Residences.keyTakeaway: Cited as a counter-example for smooth refunds and a better lift-to-flat ratio than nearby projects.

positive: A brother's repeat-purchase experience is cited approvingly in the refund-complaint thread — a prior Epitome booking cancellation (loan not sanctioned in time) was refunded after the required process.
Epitome.keyTakeaway: A repeat buyer's refund (loan not sanctioned in time) processed smoothly, cited approvingly by their sibling.

positive: The month's Folium answers consistently cite concrete due-diligence points — RWA formally handed over, e-Khata progressing, a realistic ~2.9% net rental yield, active occupancy observed on weekend visits, and an active/maintained kids' play area — used to reassure buyers wary of older Phase 1 threads, plus repeated use as the go-to delivered-project benchmark for still-under-construction projects.
A "Phase 1 vs Phase 2 possession" question directly addresses this: Phase 1 had documented delays and post-possession issues, but current Phase 2 owners report those largely resolved.
negative: Phase 1's e-Khata delays and post-possession issues are repeatedly cited as the specific history buyers should ask about before treating a Phase 2 review as representative.
Folium.keyTakeaway: Concrete due-diligence points (RWA handover, ~2.9% yield, active occupancy) make it the go-to delivered-project benchmark.

positive: Cited for a better lift-to-flat ratio and fuller backup-power coverage in builder-comparison answers.
Capitol Residences.keyTakeaway: Cited for a better lift-to-flat ratio and fuller backup-power coverage in builder-comparison answers.

positive: Rated favorably on carpet-area efficiency and amenity-cost bundling across two separate Panathur-corridor questions.
negative: Peak-hour traffic at the corridor level is flagged consistently as the one drawback.
Elysium.keyTakeaway: Favorable on carpet-area efficiency and amenity-cost bundling; peak-hour traffic is the one consistent drawback.

positive: Cited approvingly in a carpet-vs-community-amenities question for visibly active weekend occupancy (busy play area, courts in use).
Epitome.keyTakeaway: Cited approvingly for visibly active weekend occupancy — busy play area and courts in use.

positive: A site-visit question about Phase 2 near the airport drew due-diligence answers on resale demand depth and realistic rental-yield assumptions (2.5-3% net), plus a tip to check the entrance road at both 8:30am and 7pm rather than only during the sales-arranged visit.
